title: Anatomically vs. eLectrophysIologically Guided Contact SelectioN in Deep Brain Stimulation for Parkinson’s Disease
summary: Prospective single-center study comparing adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS) and anatomy-based continuous stimulation (aicDBS) in a randomized, blinded crossover design.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinically established diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease
Bilateral implantation of directional electrodes for deep brain stimulation in the subthalamic nucleus at least 10 weeks prior to study start
Stimulation system capable of adaptive stimulation (Medtronic Percept RC/PC)
Oral and written informed consent
Stable Parkinson’s disease–specific medication for at least two weeks prior to study start
Exclusion criteria:
Clinically relevant cognitive impairment
Levodopa dysregulation syndrome
Severe affective disorder
Inability or unwillingness to independently switch stimulation programs using the patient controller
Insufficient image quality of perioperative clinical imaging (cMRI/cCT) for reconstruction of the individual electrode position
